data.topic: Recognizing and Creating Patterns: extend AB patterns with colors, shapes, or sounds
data.subject: General

hook.content: Imagine you are stringing colorful beads to make a special necklace, putting on a red bead, then a blue bead, then a red bead, and then a blue bead!
hook.question: What bead color comes next on your necklace?
hook.imagePrompt: A wooden table with colorful craft beads scattered on it under bright sunlight.

bigIdea.statement: Patterns are things that repeat in a special order, like red, blue, red, blue.
bigIdea.whyItMatters: Seeing patterns helps us guess what comes next in games, music, stories, and everyday life!

objectives.text: Copy and extend a simple AB pattern using colors or shapes
Identify what comes next in a sound or movement pattern

shouldKnow: Name basic colors like red, blue, yellow, and green
Recognize simple shapes like circles and squares
Sort objects by color or shape into groups

quickCheck.question: What color is this apple? Can you find another object with that same color?
quickCheck.answer: Red, and another red object like a block or crayon.
quickCheck.hint: Look at things around the room that match the color of a ripe apple!

roadmap.description: Discover repeating patterns hiding all around us.
activities: Spot patterns in clothing and pictures

roadmap.description: See how AB patterns work with colors and shapes.
Figure out what comes next in fun pattern lines.
activities: Complete missing shapes in a row
Clap and stomp along with sound patterns

roadmap.description: Create your very own pattern to show a friend.

buildingFrom: Sorting and matching objects by attributes
Observing similarities and differences in everyday items
leadingTo: Predicting story events and daily schedules
realWorld: Floor tiles and fence posts repeating in a row

mindset.encouragement: Patterns can sometimes trick our brains at first, but with a little practice, you will spot them everywhere!
mindset.growthTip: Say the pattern out loud to yourself—hearing the rhythm makes it much easier to know what comes next.

data.today: We will copy and make fun AB patterns using colors and shapes.

wonders.text: I wonder why zebras have stripe patterns?
I wonder how music makes patterns with sounds?
I wonder what pattern I can build with my toys?
